newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FOCUS-J.Martins seen bidding for Vidago.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-J.Martins seen bidding for Vidago.

text.p: Portugal's second biggest retailer Jeronimo Martins is likely to launch a public offer to buy mineral water group Vidago in the coming days, analysts said on Friday.
"Jeronimo Martins likes to buy into businesses that are growing," said one analyst, who asked not to be identified.
Another Lisbon-based analyst said: "Water consumption is a growth market in Portugal and has a lot of potential. I think it's probable Jeronimo Martins will make an offer."
Jeronimo Martins said on Thursday it was studying the possibility of making a bid for Vidago, but that no final decision had been made.
Vidago is Portugal's leading supplier of sparkling drinking water.
One analyst said Jeronimo Martins had said at a recent meeting with his brokerage that it was interested in acquiring a mineral water company.

Vidago shares, suspended for much of this week amid the takeover talk, resumed trade on Lisbon bourse on Friday at a record high of 3,550 escudos, up 650, before easing back to 3,410 escudos, up 510, in the early afternoon.

Analysts contacted by Reuters said they believed Jeronimo Martins would offer goodwill in the deal, perhaps bidding more than 4,000 escudos per share. A bid at 4,000 escudos per share would value Vidago at some 15 billion escudos ($100 million).
"The price Jeronimo Martins will offer will be a strategic price," said one Portuguese analyst. "It will have no direct link to the value of the business right now," he added.
Analysts said they believed Jeronimo Martins could make a bid in the coming days, depending on the progress of negotiations between the two companies.
Diario de Noticias newspaper said on Friday that it had learned that negotiations had been held up by discussion of guarantees sought by Jeronimo Martins in the deal.
Analysts believed there was a slim chance a rival bidder such as beer company Unicer could emerge at the last minute.
"Unicer has the financial muscle to make a bid as it wants to diversify from beer into water," said one analyst.

Jeronimo Martins had shown that it can manage the businesses it acquires well, notably its recent acquisitions of a chain of cash-and-carry shops in Poland and the sports goods group Lillywhites in Britain, analysts said.
The company said on Thursday both acquisitions had a positive impact on its nine-month profit which showed a 48 percent year-on-year increase to 7.3 billion escudos ($48 million).
